text: Here's how Rao Fang works, in one minute.

Everything runs in the browser. Whisper tiny turns speech into text, a multilingual e5 model turns it into embeddings, and small linear heads pick the topics and sentiment. Results fill fixed Thai templates, so there's no generated text.
To train it, Claude acted as the teacher, writing and labelling 1,832 guest comments in four languages, kept only when a blind re-check agreed. A small student learned from them on a CPU, in minutes.
Anything uncertain goes to a person. On held-out synthetic data, that leaves sixty-nine percent sorted automatically, at ninety-one percent precision.
It's an installable web app. The models download once, then it works in airplane mode, with all data kept on the device.
So far, it's tested on synthetic data and an emulated phone. Next: a real phone, and real guests.
